facts.question: What do satellites see on the last clear days, and does it match the snow model?

en.title: 120 cm at Manning Park Resort: western Canada's depth leader
en.description: Manning Park leads western Canada with 120 cm on November 13, 34 cm ahead of Big White, confirmed by early November satellite observations.
en.lede: 120 cm at Manning Park Resort puts it 34 cm ahead of Big White in western Canada. When satellites last saw clear skies in early November, they confirmed snow cover across every resort in this analysis; our model's depth estimates today align with those observations.

p: Manning Park Resort tops western Canada with 120 cm depth at upper slopes—a substantial 34 cm margin over Big White at 86 cm. What makes this lead surprising is elevation: Manning Park's summit sits at only 1,789 m, while Big White reaches 2,271 m. In typical mountain snow patterns, higher elevation means deeper snow; Manning Park breaks this rule. Local wind or orographic effects have likely favoured its slopes.

The rest of the ranking is clear: Big White at 86 cm, Marmot Basin and Revelstoke both near 53–54 cm, and Tweedsmuir at 45 cm. These are model estimates for November 13, based on our analysis of snow data and weather patterns from recent days.

sections.h: What satellites saw when clouds cleared
p: To test whether these depths are realistic, we turn to satellite observations. On November 4, when clouds broke, satellites saw snow covering Manning Park, Big White, Marmot Basin, and Revelstoke. Tweedsmuir Ski Club appeared on a fresh satellite pass on November 10, also snow-covered. These are direct observations from space, not estimates.
They confirm one crucial fact: snow is actually there at all five resorts. That satellite evidence is vital for validating our model.

sections.h: Model and satellite data in agreement
p: Our depth estimates align with the satellite observations. Satellites confirmed snow was present across the region in early November; our model now estimates how much. Manning Park's lead is not an artefact of the model—the model is capturing real differences in snowfall and elevation between these sites. The gradient from 120 cm down to 45 cm is plausible for early November.

The key limitation: cloud has covered the region since November 4 and 10, so we cannot see the current state from space. Our depth estimates today are based on the model, not fresh satellite data. That satellite validation from early November gives us confidence to forecast forward.

sections.h: Revelstoke and Big White gain ground in the forecast
p: The model forecasts substantial snow for November 14 to 16, and rankings will shift. Revelstoke is expected to receive 21 cm, the most in the region. Big White will see 16 cm, Marmot Basin 3 cm, and Tweedsmuir 4 cm. Manning Park, despite its current lead, is forecast only 10 cm—not enough to maintain its 34 cm margin.

By November 16, the depth rankings will likely change, with Revelstoke possibly moving into contention for the lead. Cloud cover will make satellite confirmation of these changes difficult; we will rely on the model and ground reports for the next week.

Zoom out from these five resorts. As of November 13, snow covers 201,390 km² of western Canada, with snow present at 31 of 57 resorts. That is down from November 11, when 35 resorts reported snow and coverage reached 215,390 km². However, the forecast expects recovery to around 210,000 km² and 35 active resorts by November 16 as fresh snow arrives.
This is the classic early-November pattern: uneven coverage, modest depths, and advantage favouring elevation gain.

advice: Manning Park has the region's best current depth at 120 cm, but early-season snow is thin off main slopes—stick to groomed upper terrain.
Revelstoke is forecast 21 cm by November 16, which could rival Manning Park; watch the forecast closely if you plan to ski there.
Big White sits second at 86 cm with 16 cm forecast; it will gain ground but likely stay behind Manning Park and Revelstoke.
Early-season snowpack is thin across western Canada. Consult your area's official avalanche bulletin before skiing off-piste.
Satellite observations confirmed snow is present at all major resorts, but depths carry early-November uncertainty; the forecast is your best guide for the next week.
